events.title: Perl 5.0 released
events.summary: Larry Wall released Perl 5.0 on October 17, 1994 — a complete rewrite adding objects, references, modules, and the CPAN ecosystem foundation.
events.about: Perl 5 became the duct tape of the early web: CGI scripts, system administration, bioinformatics, and text munging. The module system and CPAN let developers share libraries decades before npm or PyPI — powering everything from Slashdot to early Amazon glue code.

narrative.whyChosen: Perl 5 defined scripting culture for the 1990s web and Unix automation.
narrative.whyImportant: Objects, references, and CPAN made Perl a platform, not just a language.
narrative.problemSolved: Perl 4 could not scale to complex programs; the web needed a richer scripting language with reusable libraries.
